stem: Which constitutional issue was President Lincoln addressing in this excerpt?

options.label: F
options.text: The right of citizens to choose representatives

options.label: G
options.text: The power of states to organize militias

options.label: J
options.text: The legal ability of states to secede

visual_elements: The States have their status in the Union, and they have no other legal status. . . . The Union, and not themselves separately, procured their independence and their liberty. —President Abraham Lincoln, message to Congress, July 4, 1861
